summary: A note from the University of Illinois on making mathematical software libraries available over the ARPANET. It lists projects such as the Bell Labs library, IMSL and NATS, and suggests that the network could make such libraries shareable resources. It discusses what stands in the way.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 382 suggests treating mathematical software libraries as resources that network users could share. The University of Illinois planned to obtain the NATS library and make it available on several computers.

subtitle: Sharing mathematical software libraries through the network

tldr.problem: Mathematical and statistical software libraries existed at several institutions, and researchers could benefit from sharing information about them.
tldr.mechanism: The author proposes making the NATS library available on several network-connected IBM and PDP-10 computers, with the project's cooperation.
tldr.outcome: The notice invites information about other users' experience with mathematical and statistical libraries.

today: RFC 382 is a proposal to share mathematical software and information about it across the ARPA Network. Its text describes an intended NATS installation, not a completed deployment.

sections.title: Existing Mathematical Libraries
sections.content: Lawrence McDaniel lists several efforts to build mathematical and statistical subroutine libraries: a Bell Laboratories project, IMSL Library I, and the NATS project involving the National Science Foundation, Argonne Laboratories, Stanford and Texas. NATS worked on the Wilkinson linear algebra routines.
sections.plainLanguage: Several institutions had developed collections of mathematical programs. The notice names Bell Laboratories, IMSL and the NATS project.

sections.title: The Network as a Shared Resource
sections.content: The author suggests that the ARPA Network could make mathematical libraries another shareable resource. He recognizes that different computers may need different software and that people may prefer different tools, but argues that exchanging information about the libraries could still benefit users.
sections.plainLanguage: Network access could help researchers use or learn about libraries held elsewhere. Different computers and preferences would still matter.

sections.title: The University of Illinois Plan
sections.content: The University of Illinois planned to obtain the NATS library and, with the project's cooperation, make it available on several network IBM 360/370 and PDP-10 computers. McDaniel invites readers to share their experiences with the mathematical and statistical libraries named in the note.
sections.plainLanguage: Illinois intended to get the NATS library and offer it on several network computers. The author also asked readers to report their experience with such software.
